free_tier.stated: No free tier and no trial named: "Standard ... $7/ month" and "Enterprise ... Custom".

egress.terms: No transfer allowance and no rate is published on the homepage. The comparison table lists architecture only, and "Zero traffic logs" is a logging claim rather than a quota.; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: Dashboard provisioning; no API named on the page read.
chaining: One address with every port open replaces a port-mapped tunnel and a reverse proxy at once.

limits.value: 10 IPv4 addresses maximum on Standard, at USD 3 each

binding_note: No allowance is published, so 1 TiB/month meets an unknown policy rather than a number. The address count is the documented limit: one address at USD 7 and up to nine more at USD 3.

identity_cost.detail: A paid dashboard signup ("Reserve an IP"); the signup form was not read. The operator describes itself as a Public Benefit Corporation.

reliability_note: Edge scrubbing is included; no uptime figure is published for the Standard tier.
confidence_note: Price, port range, protocol and the 1:1 mapping are first-party. Volume is the open field, and a support email is what would close it.

evidence.proved: USD 7/month for one dedicated IPv4 with up to 65,535 TCP and UDP ports; additional IPs at USD 3 up to ten; WireGuard tunnel; DDoS scrubbing included; no bandwidth figure

price_per_tb_month: USD 7 per month for one IPv4; USD 3 per month for each additional address up to ten
notes: The 65,535-port claim is the widest and is stated as a footnoted promise. The vendor's differentiator is address migration across a router fabric rather than a single tunnel server, which matters for uptime but not for volume.

extras.wg_detail: The address is mapped one to one over a tunnel: "A public IPv4 delivered through an encrypted WireGuard tunnel and mapped 1:1 to your device." Provisioning is a dashboard action: "Provisioned in under a minute from the dashboard", and the port range is the selling point: "Bind up to 65,535 TCP and UDP ports".
extras.volume_stated: No transfer allowance and no rate is published on the homepage. The comparison table lists architecture only, and "Zero traffic logs" is a logging claim rather than a quota.
extras.transit_note: BGP-managed ingress from the vendor's own edge fabric, six regions.
